My child who feels shy at Grandma's house

When you visit Grandma's for a holiday or vacation, she welcomes them warmly, yet your child hangs back bashfully and hides behind Mom. And a question like "When are we going home?" can leave the grown-ups feeling a little hurt.

When they don't get to visit often, Grandma and Grandpa's place can feel like an unfamiliar space to your child. But with just a little shared love, that unfamiliarity turns into the fondest feeling in the world.

Curious about the grandma storybook? Take a look at its lessons alongside the illustrations. Meet the key scenes of the story too. Read it together with your child and talk it over. From a grandparents storybook to a countryside grandma's house storybook and a family storybook recommendation, we've gathered many stories around 42. Grandma's the Best — Snuggle Right In!
content.caption: It's natural to feel shy when you rarely visit. Love turns it into fondness.

content.alt: 42. Grandma's the Best — Snuggle Right In! - Why time with grandparents is so precious
content.text:
Why time with grandparents is so precious

Time spent with grandparents lets a child experience a 'wider love.' Being loved without limit in a way that's different from a parent's love nurtures your child's sense of emotional security.

And a countryside grandma's house is a gift of nature—garden plots, soil, ripening fruit—things hard to come by in the city. The bond that connects the generations and the experience of nature become warm memories that stay in a child's heart for a long time.
content.caption: A grandparent's love and the experience of nature stay in a child's heart for a long time.

content.text:
Hori's story of growing fond of the country house

In 『Grandma's the Best — Snuggle Right In!』, Hori feels awkward and glum in the unfamiliar country house. Just then Grandma hands him a steaming baked sweet potato, and Grandpa lets him pick tomatoes from the garden.

When Hori realizes they've been getting ready for him for days, his heart swells and he snuggles right into Grandma's arms. On the day they leave, he's so sad that tears spring to his eyes. Along with Hori, your child feels that 'when you share love, unfamiliarity becomes fondness.'
content.caption: His heart swelled at the love they'd prepared for days.

content.alt: 42. Grandma's the Best — Snuggle Right In! - How to get ready for a visit to Grandma's
content.text:
How to get ready for a visit to Grandma's

A few days before the visit, read this book together and plant some anticipation: "Grandma says she's waiting for us!" When the unfamiliarity is eased in advance, your child warms up far more easily.

At Grandma's house, create a small job only your child can do—picking tomatoes, a walk around the yard. After you come home, ask "What did you like best at Grandma's?" and relive the good memories together; that makes the next visit even more anticipated.
content.caption: A small role and good memories make the next visit something to look forward to.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions

Q. Why is a relationship with grandparents good for my child?

A. Grandma and Grandpa's warm love becomes a sturdy emotional fence for your child. The experience of snuggling in and exchanging love nurtures a generous heart.

Q. How does a grandma storybook help?

A. Watching the main character share affection with Grandma, your child feels the family's love even more deeply. A grandma storybook conveys the warm heart that connects the generations.

Q. How can we stay close to grandparents we rarely see?

A. Share your feelings often through video calls or letters, and make joyful memories when you do meet. As time spent expressing love adds up, your hearts grow close even from afar.
